sub_agendas_items.title: PWIC-2026-07 – Project coordination
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by: Councillor L. Johnson
Residents are very concerned about the perceived lack of coordination between City of Ottawa construction projects, as well as with projects managed by 3rd parties like power and telecommunications utilities and projects managed by senior levels of government such as MTO and the NCC.
My office has been informed many times that City project managers were unaware of other City or 3rd party projects until we brought it to their attention. Lack of coordination is costly to the city because of the need to implement last-minute solutions like traffic calming, notifications, and even duplicated work like repaving.
The City formerly used software called enVista to help manage some projects, and is now developing the application of Land Management Software (LMS) as part of an update to the Municipal Application Partnership (MAP) software. The rollout of LMS/MAP is apparently not yet complete.

sub_agendas_items.title: PWIC-2026-08 - Signalized Intersections Turn Signals
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by: Councillor W. Lo
Across the City, newly signalised intersections typically receive a basic set of signals with no turning signals. Often, these intersections eventually require retrofits as traffic volumes increase with community growth or even changes in traffic patterns. Some retrofits happen years after initial installation, while others happen after a short amount of time.

sub_agendas_items.title: Motion – L. Dudas – Left turning signal phasing at Oleans Blvd and St. Joseph Blvd

motions.motion_text:
That the rules of procedure be waived to consider the matter below at the August 27, 2026 meeting of Public Works and Infrastructure Committee.
WHEREAS local residents have raised ongoing concerns regarding vehicles making a left turn from eastbound St. Joseph Boulevard onto northbound Orléans Boulevard; and
WHEREAS staff have reviewed the location for permissive/protected signal phasing and it did not meet the required warrants for installation in the eastbound direction; and
WHEREAS staff have confirmed that network screening determined that eastbound and westbound left-turn collisions at this intersection are over-represented and therefore would benefit from the implementation of fully-protected left-turn signal phasing; and
WHEREAS fully-protected left-turn signal phasing eliminates conflicts with opposing traffic movements, significantly reducing the frequency of left-turn collisions; and
WHEREAS a preliminary operational review by Traffic Services staff has already determined that implementing fully-protected left-turn signal phasing at this location requires physical changes to the intersection; and
WHEREAS functional planning, design and construction of physical changes required for implementation of fully protected left turns is funded by the Road Safety Action Plan when locations have been identified through the established network screening process; and
WHEREAS there are a number of locations identified through network screening for fully protected lefts that are awaiting funding; and
WHEREAS the Road Safety Action Plan budget has been impacted by the loss of revenue associated with the cancellation of the Automated Speed Enforcement program; and
WHEREAS resolving the eastbound left-turn concerns at St. Joseph Boulevard and Orléans Boulevard remains one of the most frequently requested traffic improvements in Ward 2;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Traffic Services be directed to undertake the necessary functional planning work to determine the specific physical changes required to implement eastbound and westbound fully-protected left-turn signal phasing at the intersection of St. Joseph Boulevard and Orléans Boulevard as expediently as possible; and
THEREFORE BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff be directed to provide regular updates to the Ward 2 Councillor on this work.
